Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

from collections import Counter
def solve(patt):
    h,w=len(patt),len(patt[0])
    # determine period: find row/col periods from structure
    # assume period p such that pattern repeats; detect via first differing offsets
    def period(arr):
        n=len(arr); per=None
        for p in range(1,n):
            if all(arr[i]==arr[(i+p)%n] for i in range(n)): per=p; break
        return per
    rp=period([r[0] for r in patt]) if False else None
    # detect: rows that are constant -> separator rows; use gaps
    const_rows=[r for r in range(h) if all(x==patt[r][0] for x in patt[r])]
    cr=[c for c in range(w) if all(patt[r][c]==patt[0][c] for r in range(h))]
    # block size: distance between separators
    def sep_periods(seps):
        return sorted(set(b-a for a,b in zip(seps+[-1],seps+[h-1]))) if seps else (h,w)
    print('const rows',const_rows,'const cols',cr)
    return patt

from collections import Counter
def solve(di):
    h,w=len(di),len(di[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for row in di for x in row)
    tile=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    # separator color: second most common
    items=cnt.most_common()
    sep=items[1][0] if len(items)>1 else items[0][0]
    # h-lines: rows with >= w-5 cells of sep color
    hL=[r for r in range(h) if sum(1 for x in di[r] if x==sep)>=w-5]
    vL=[c for c in range(w) if sum(1 for r in range(h) if di[r][c]==sep)>=h-5]
    anom=[[False]*(w) for _ in range(h)]
    for r in hL:
        for c in range(w):
            if di[r][c]!=sep: anom[r][c]=True
    for c in vL:
        for r in range(h):
            if di[r][c]!=sep: anom[r][c]=True
    amin=min(r for r in hL if any(anom[r]))
    amax=max(r for r in hL if any(anom[r]))
    bmin=min(c for c in vL if any(anom[r][c] for r in range(h)))
    bmax=max(c for c in vL if any(anom[r][c] for r in range(h)))
    Bh=sorted([r for r in hL if amin<=r<=amax])
    Bv=sorted([c for c in vL if bmin<=c<=bmax])
    out=[]
    for i in range(len(Bh)-1):
        row=[]
        for j in range(len(Bv)-1):
            cs=[di[Bh[i+k]][Bv[j+l]] for k in (0,1) for l in (0,1)]
            row.append(cs[0] if len(set(cs))==1 and cs[0]!=sep else tile)
        out.append(row)
    return out
for n in (1,2,3):
    pred=solve(G[f'Demo pair {n} input'])
    exp=G[f'Demo pair {n} output']
    print(n, pred==exp, pred, exp)
print(solve(G['Test input']))
